questions.question: As per the World Happiness Index 2023, which of the following countries secured the highest rank?

• Nepal's focus on **well-being, traditional values, and environmental sustainability** has contributed to its higher ranking on the index.

 __

questions.question: Atmospheric temperature usually decreases with altitude, but sometimes this phenomenon gets reversed in the troposphere. This phenomenon is known as ________.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Temperature Inversion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Temperature Inversion** occurs when the normal pattern of temperature decrease with altitude is reversed, meaning the air temperature increases with height in a layer of the atmosphere, particularly in the **troposphere.**
 
• This phenomenon is typically observed during **calm weather conditions**, especially in winter when the ground cools rapidly overnight.
 
• It is most common during **clear nights** when the Earth's surface loses heat quickly, leading to a layer of cooler air trapped beneath a layer of warmer air.
 
• Temperature inversions can cause **air pollution** as they trap pollutants like smog and particulate matter close to the ground.
 
• Inversions often lead to **poor visibility** and can impact health due to reduced air quality.
 
• Such conditions are significant in areas with high industrial activity or vehicular emissions, as the pollutants cannot disperse easily.
 
• A temperature inversion can also affect **weather patterns**, such as suppressing cloud formation and limiting precipitation.
 
• Examples of regions where temperature inversion is a frequent occurrence include large cities like **Delhi** and **Los Angeles**, which face challenges of air pollution due to inversion layers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Adiabatic Lapse Rate**__

 __
 
• The **Adiabatic Lapse Rate** refers to the rate of temperature change with altitude under conditions where no heat is exchanged between the air and its surroundings.
 
• The rate is different for **dry air** and **moist air**. For dry air, the typical lapse rate is approximately **9.8°C per kilometer.**
 
• This is a fundamental concept in meteorology and helps explain phenomena such as cloud formation and atmospheric stability.
 
 
 
• **Global Warming**__
 __
 
• **Global Warming** refers to the long-term increase in Earth's average surface temperature due to human activities, primarily the emission of **greenhouse gases** like carbon dioxide and methane.
 
• This phenomenon is unrelated to the localized temperature inversion discussed here.
 
• The effects of global warming include **melting glaciers, rising sea levels, and extreme weather events.**
 
 
 
• **Temperature Convection**__
 
 
• **Temperature Convection** involves the transfer of heat through the movement of fluids (liquids or gases), driven by differences in temperature and density.
 
• This is a common process in the atmosphere, where warm air rises and cooler air sinks, leading to phenomena such as **wind formation** and cloud development.
 
• Unlike temperature inversion, convection facilitates mixing of air layers rather than trapping them.

questions.question: What is the name of the German Chancellor who visited India in February 2023?

questions.question: As per the Constitution of India, every Governor, before entering upon his office, will make and subscribe an oath in the presence of the ________.

options.text: Chief Justice of the High Court

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Chief Justice of the High Court**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per **Article 159** of the **Indian Constitution**, every Governor, before assuming office, is required to make and subscribe an **oath or affirmation of office**.
 
• The oath or affirmation is administered by the **Chief Justice of the High Court** of the concerned state or, in his/her absence, by the senior-most Judge of that court.
 
• This provision ensures that the Governor pledges to preserve, protect, and defend the **Constitution** and the law.
 
• The oath includes a commitment to faithfully execute the duties of the office and to serve the people to the best of their abilities.
 
• The role of the **Chief Justice of the High Court** in administering the oath emphasizes the independence of the judiciary and its role in upholding the constitutional framework.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chief Minister**__

 __
 
• The **Chief Minister** is the head of the government in a state but does not have the constitutional authority to administer the oath of office to the Governor.
 
• The Governor, in fact, administers the oath of office to the Chief Minister and other ministers in the state.
 
 
 
• **President**__
 __
 
• The **President of India** appoints the Governor under **Article 155** of the Constitution, but the President does not administer the oath of office to the Governor.
 
• The President's role is limited to the appointment and removal of the Governor.
 
 
 
• **Chief Justice of India**__
 
 
• The **Chief Justice of India** administers the oath of office to the President of India and not to the Governor.
 
• The Chief Justice of India is the head of the judiciary system in the country and deals with constitutional matters at the national level.

questions.question: ‘Alarippu’ is the first dance item of which of the following Indian classical dance forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **‘Alarippu’** is an invocatory piece and the first dance item performed in the classical Indian dance form of **Bharatanatyam**.
 
• The term **‘Alarippu’** means "to bloom" or "to unfold," symbolizing the awakening of the body, mind, and spirit in preparation for the performance.
 
• It is performed as a pure **nritta** (abstract dance) piece, focusing on rhythmic movements without any interpretative expressions or storytelling.
 
• The primary purpose of ‘Alarippu’ is to pay respect to the **stage, audience, and guru** while invoking blessings for the performance.
 
• Bharatanatyam originated in the temples of **Tamil Nadu** and is known for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, intricate footwork, and gestures or **mudras** that convey emotions.
 
• The sequence of a Bharatanatyam performance typically follows a traditional order, starting with **‘Alarippu’**, followed by pieces like **Jatiswaram, Varnam, Padam, and Tillana**.
 
• Bharatanatyam is one of the **oldest classical dance forms in India** and is deeply rooted in the Natya Shastra, an ancient treatise on performing arts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kuchipudi**__

 __
 
• **Kuchipudi** is a classical dance form originating from **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• It involves a combination of **nritta (pure dance), nritya (expressive dance), and natya (dramatic art)**.
 
• Kuchipudi performances often include a dramatic narrative with dialogues, and dancers typically play multiple roles in a story.
 
 
 
• **Kathakali**__
 __
 
• **Kathakali** originates from **Kerala** and is known for its elaborate makeup, colorful costumes, and face masks.
 
• It is a dance-drama form that typically depicts stories from the **Ramayana, Mahabharata, and Puranas**.
 
• Performances are highly theatrical and require rigorous physical training.
 
 
 
• **Odissi**__
 
 
• **Odissi** is a classical dance form that originated in the temples of **Odisha**.
 
• It is characterized by its fluid movements, graceful postures, and the **tribhangi** (three-bend posture).
 
• Odissi emphasizes both **nritta** (pure dance) and **abhinaya** (expressive dance).

questions.question: The Tunga and Bhadra are tributaries of which river?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Krishna River**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Tunga** and **Bhadra** rivers are important tributaries of the **Krishna River**.
 
• The **Tunga River** originates from the **Western Ghats** near **Gangamoola in Chikmagalur district, Karnataka.**
 
• The **Bhadra River** also originates from the **Western Ghats** near **Gangamoola, Karnataka**, and flows through the state before merging with the Tunga River.
 
• These two rivers join at **Koodli** in Karnataka to form the **Tungabhadra River**, which is a major tributary of the Krishna River.
 
• The Krishna River is one of the longest rivers in India, with its origin in the **Mahabaleshwar region of Maharashtra**, and flows through the states of **Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh.**
 
• The Krishna River ultimately empties into the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
• It is one of the **most important rivers in southern India**, playing a crucial role in **agriculture and irrigation.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Narmada River**__

 __
 
• The **Narmada River** is one of the major rivers in central India.
 
• It originates from the **Amarkantak Plateau** in Madhya Pradesh.
 
• The Narmada flows westward and empties into the **Arabian Sea**.
 
• It is often referred to as the **"Lifeline of Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat."**
 
 
 
• **Tapti River**__
 __
 
• The **Tapti River** originates from the **Satpura range** in Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It flows through the states of **Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Gujarat** before meeting the **Arabian Sea.**
 
• The Tapti is one of the **three rivers in peninsular India** that flows westward, the others being the Narmada and Mahi rivers.
 
 
 
• **Godavari River**__
 
 
• The **Godavari** is the **largest river** in Peninsular India and is often referred to as the **"Dakshin Ganga."**
 
• The river originates in the **Nasik district of Maharashtra** and flows eastward into the **Bay of Bengal.**
 
• The Godavari has several tributaries, including the **Penganga, Indravati, Pranhita, and Manjira rivers.**

questions.question: When did India declare itself a Sovereign, Democratic and Republic state with the adoption of the Constitution?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**26 January 1950.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India declared itself a **Sovereign, Democratic, and Republic state** on **January 26, 1950**, with the formal adoption of its **Constitution**.
 
• This day is celebrated as **Republic Day** every year to commemorate the implementation of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• The Indian Constitution was drafted by the **Constituent Assembly**, chaired by **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**, who is also known as the **Father of the Indian Constitution**.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written constitution** of any sovereign country in the world.
 
• On this date, the **Government of India Act 1935**, which was the governing law under British rule, was replaced by the newly adopted **Constitution of India**.
 
• The choice of **January 26** was significant, as it was on this date in **1930** that the **Purna Swaraj (Complete Independence) Declaration** was made by the Indian National Congress.
 
• The Constitution provides for key features such as **secularism, socialism, democracy, federalism, and fundamental rights** for its citizens.
 
• The day highlights India's transition to a fully sovereign state, emphasizing its independence from British dominion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 list of features borrowed by the Indian Constitution

 
• Fundamental Rights - Borrowed from the U.S. Constitution.
 
• Directive Principles of State Policy - Borrowed from the Irish Constitution.
 
• Emergency Provisions - Borrowed from the Weimar Constitution (Germany).
 
• Bicameral Legislature - Borrowed from the British Parliament.
 
• Parliamentary System of Government - Borrowed from the British Constitution.
 
• Judicial Review - Borrowed from the U.S. Constitution.
 
• Fundamental Duties - Borrowed from the USSR Constitution.
 
• Independent Judiciary - Borrowed from the U.S. Constitution.
 
• Single Citizenship - Borrowed from the British Constitution.
 
• Nominal and Real Executives - Borrowed from the British Constitution.

questions.question: Diwan-i-Am, containing the marble canopy ornamented with beautiful panels of pietra dura work, is a part of which monument?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Red Fort**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Diwan-i-Am** is located within the premises of the **Red Fort** in Delhi.
 
• This hall was used by the Mughal emperors for **public audiences** and addressing grievances from the general public.
 
• The structure contains a **marble canopy** adorned with intricate **panels of pietra dura work**, showcasing exquisite craftsmanship.
 
• The **Red Fort**, built by Emperor **Shah Jahan** in 1639, served as the main residence of the Mughal emperors for nearly 200 years.
 
• The fort is constructed using **red sandstone**, giving it its distinctive name.
 
• The **Red Fort** is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (2007) and is an iconic monument in India, symbolizing the nation's rich history.
 
• The fort includes several significant structures such as the **Diwan-i-Am, Diwan-i-Khas, Rang Mahal, and Moti Masjid.**
 
• The **Prime Minister of India** hoists the **national flag** at the Red Fort on Independence Day every year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bibi ka Maqbara**__

 __
 
• **Bibi ka Maqbara**, located in **Aurangabad, Maharashtra**, was commissioned by **Emperor Aurangzeb** in memory of his mother, Dilras Banu Begum.
 
• It is often referred to as the **"Taj of the Deccan"** due to its resemblance to the Taj Mahal.
 
• The monument reflects a blend of **Mughal architectural style**.
 
 
 
• **Taj Mahal**__
 __
 
• The **Taj Mahal**, located in **Agra**, was built by Emperor **Shah Jahan** in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
 
• It is recognized as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** and one of the **Seven Wonders of the World**.
 
• The monument is famous for its **white marble construction and intricate pietra dura work.**
 
 
 
• **Humayun Tomb**__
 
 
• **Humayun's Tomb**, located in **Delhi**, was commissioned by **Empress Bega Begum**, the wife of Emperor Humayun.
 
• The tomb is known for its **Mughal architecture** and is regarded as a precursor to the Taj Mahal.
 
• It is also a **UNESCO World Heritage Site declared in 1993**.

questions.question: Which of the following is a crop grown in Rabi season in India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Wheat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Wheat** is a major **Rabi crop** grown in India.
 
• Rabi crops are generally sown in the **winter season** (October to December) and harvested during the **spring season** (April to June).
 
• **Wheat** requires a **cool climate** and **moderate rainfall** during its growing period, with a warm and sunny environment during the harvesting phase.
 
• It is primarily cultivated in the northern and northwestern parts of India, including states like **Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• India is the **second-largest producer of wheat** in the world, contributing significantly to global production.
 
• The crop is a staple food in India, used to prepare products like **chapati, bread, biscuits, and other bakery items.**
 
• The introduction of the **Green Revolution** in the 1960s significantly boosted wheat production in India, especially in the Indo-Gangetic Plain.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Soyabean**__

 __
 
• **Soyabean** is a **Kharif crop**, which means it is grown during the **monsoon season** (June to September).
 
• It requires a warm climate with moderate to high rainfall.
 
• India’s major soyabean-growing states include **Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Rajasthan.**
 
• Soyabean is an important source of **protein and oil** and is used in making products like **soy milk, tofu, and animal feed.**
 
 
 
• **Maize**__
 __
 
• **Maize** is primarily a **Kharif crop**, though it is also grown in the Rabi season in some areas under irrigation.
 
• It is cultivated in states like **Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Uttar Pradesh.**
 
• Maize is a versatile crop used for **human consumption, animal feed, and industrial purposes.**
 
 
 
• **Rice**__
 
 
• **Rice** is predominantly a **Kharif crop** in India, requiring abundant water and warm temperatures for cultivation.
 
• It is widely grown in the **eastern, southern, and northeastern regions** of India, with states like **West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, and Andhra Pradesh** being major producers.
 
• Rice is the **staple food** for a significant portion of the Indian population.

questions.question: The 'Secular' word in the Indian Constitution was added to the constitution by ________ Constitutional Amendment Act.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**42nd Constitutional Amendment Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **'Secular'** was added to the Indian Constitution through the **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976**.
 
• This amendment inserted the terms **'Secular'** and **'Socialist'** into the Preamble of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The term **'Secular'** signifies that the Indian state has no official religion and treats all religions equally, ensuring freedom of religion for all citizens.
 
• The amendment was introduced during the tenure of **Prime Minister Indira Gandhi**.
 
• The 42nd Amendment is often referred to as the **“Mini-Constitution”** due to the extensive changes it brought to the Constitution.
 
• It also added provisions related to the **Fundamental Duties** in Part IV-A of the Constitution (Article 51A).
 
• The amendment aimed to strengthen the principles of **democracy, equality, and justice** as enshrined in the Constitution.
 
• It also made significant changes to the **structure of the judiciary**, the powers of the central and state governments, and the Directive Principles of State Policy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **44th Constitutional Amendment Act**__

 __
 
• The **44th Amendment** was enacted in **1978** to undo some of the changes made by the 42nd Amendment.
 
• It restored the **original emphasis on fundamental rights** and curtailed the powers of the executive during emergencies.
 
• This amendment ensured that **Article 21 (Right to Life and Personal Liberty)** cannot be suspended even during a national emergency.
 
 
 
• **46th Constitutional Amendment Act**__
 __
 
• The **46th Amendment**, enacted in **1982**, dealt with issues related to **sales tax** on goods and services.
 
• It included a wide range of transactions within the ambit of the term **'sale of goods'** to enable states to levy sales tax on them.
 
 
 
• **48th Constitutional Amendment Act**__
 
 
• The **48th Amendment** was passed in **1984** to extend the President's Rule in the state of **Punjab** beyond one year.
 
• This was done in the context of the prevailing situation in Punjab due to the rise of **insurgency and militancy**.

questions.question: Who among the following Portuguese travellers visited the Vijayanagar empire during the reign of Krishnadevaraya?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Domingo Paes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Domingo Paes** was a **Portuguese traveller** who visited the **Vijayanagar Empire** during the reign of **Krishnadevaraya**, one of the greatest emperors of the empire.
 
• He provided a vivid and detailed account of the **Vijayanagar Empire**, including its **administration, military, culture, and economy**.
 
• His writings are considered one of the most reliable sources of information about the **Vijayanagar Empire** during the 16th century.
 
• Paes described the **prosperity and wealth** of the empire, especially its capital, **Hampi**, which was a flourishing trade and cultural hub.
 
• He also highlighted the strong fortifications, the well-organized military, and the efficient administration under **Krishnadevaraya**.
 
• His accounts serve as an important historical source for understanding the **political and social structure** of the Vijayanagar Empire.

questions.concept: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India
questions.question: Who among the following social reformers established the ‘Prarthana Samaj’ in Bombay in 1867?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atmaram Pandurang**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Atmaram Pandurang** was a prominent social reformer and the founder of the **Prarthana Samaj** in **Bombay** in **1867.**
 
• The **Prarthana Samaj** aimed at reforming Hindu society by discarding caste-based discrimination and promoting **monotheism**.
 
• It was inspired by the teachings of the **Brahmo Samaj**, which focused on rationalism and spiritualism.
 
• Atmaram Pandurang emphasized on **abolishing child marriage**, **promoting widow remarriage**, and improving the status of women in society.
 
• The organization worked towards fostering **education, social equality, and ethical conduct** among the people.
 
• The **Prarthana Samaj** leaders were also influenced by the ideas of **Raja Ram Mohan Roy**, who was a pioneer of social reform in India.
 
• Atmaram Pandurang collaborated with other reformers like **Justice Mahadev Govind Ranade** to strengthen the movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gopal Hari Deshmukh**__

 __
 
• Known as **Lokhitwadi**, Gopal Hari Deshmukh was a social reformer and writer from Maharashtra.
 
• He advocated for **modern education**, **women’s rights**, and the abolition of caste discrimination.
 
• Though he was an important reformer, he was not associated with the founding of the **Prarthana Samaj**.
 
 
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**__
 __
 
• Tilak was a prominent **freedom fighter** and nationalist leader, known as the **"Father of Indian Unrest."**
 
• He was associated with the **Indian independence movement** and is famous for his slogan "**Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it.**"
 
• Tilak was not involved in social reform movements like the **Prarthana Samaj**.
 
 
 
• **Ganesh Agarkar**__
 
 
• Ganesh Agarkar was a **social reformer** and the first editor of the newspaper **Kesari**, started by Bal Gangadhar Tilak.
 
• He focused on **educational and social reforms**, particularly emphasizing **women’s rights**.
 
• However, he was not involved with the **Prarthana Samaj**.

questions.question: Which of the following characteristics was used by Aristotle to classify animals?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Habitat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Aristotle, known as the **"Father of Zoology"**, was one of the first scientists to classify animals systematically.
 
• He used the **habitat** of animals as a primary criterion for classification.
 
• According to Aristotle, animals could be grouped based on where they lived, such as in water, air, or on land.
 
• This classification system led to three broad groups:
 
 
• **Aquatic animals:** Animals that live in water, such as fish and whales.
 
• **Terrestrial animals:** Animals that live on land, such as lions and elephants.
 
• **Aerial animals:** Animals that live in the air, such as birds and bats.
 
 
 
• This system was a foundational concept in the study of zoology and helped in understanding the diversity of life forms.
 
• Although this method is now outdated, it laid the groundwork for modern biological classification systems, such as the Linnaean taxonomy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Specialised organs**__

 __
 
• Specialized organs refer to body parts adapted for specific functions, such as the heart for pumping blood or lungs for respiration.
 
• While Aristotle noted some anatomical differences, his primary classification was not based on the presence or absence of specialized organs.
 
• Modern taxonomy, however, does consider organ specialization in classifying species.
 
 
 
• **Types of body cells**__
 __
 
• The differentiation of body cells, such as prokaryotic vs. eukaryotic cells, was not a concept known during Aristotle's time.
 
• This characteristic became relevant only after the discovery of the cell by **Robert Hooke** in the 17th century.
 
 
 
• **Photosynthesis**__
 
 
• Photosynthesis is a process by which plants convert sunlight into energy.
 
• Since Aristotle focused on animals, photosynthesis was irrelevant to his classification system.
 
• However, this process plays a crucial role in the classification of plants in modern botany.

questions.question: The 2011 census was the ____________ official survey conducted in India.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**15th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **2011 Census** was the **15th official census** conducted in **India**.
 
• The first census in India was conducted in the year **1872** under British rule, though it wasn't a synchronous census.
 
• The first synchronous census was conducted in **1881**, and since then, it has been carried out every 10 years.
 
• India’s census is one of the **largest administrative exercises in the world**, involving the collection of demographic, economic, and social data.
 
• The 2011 Census provided crucial data on **population size, literacy rates, sex ratio**, and more, which are used for planning and development purposes.
 
• This census was conducted under the supervision of the **Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India**, a post held by **C. Chandramouli** during the 2011 census.
 
• The 2011 census was notable for including data on parameters such as **housing, household amenities, and assets**.
 
• It also marked the first time that biometric data was collected for the **National Population Register (NPR)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Takeaways from the 2011 Census:**

 
 
• The total population of India in 2011 was **1.21 billion**, accounting for approximately **17.5% of the world's population**.
 
• The literacy rate in 2011 was recorded at **74.04%**, with a significant improvement in female literacy.
 
• The sex ratio improved slightly to **940 females per 1000 males**.
 
• States like **Uttar Pradesh** had the highest population, while **Sikkim** had the lowest.
 
 
 
• **Incorrect Options:**
 
 
• 16th:__ Refers to the upcoming census (2021 Census), which has been delayed due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• __14th:__ Refers to the 2001 Census, which preceded the 2011 Census and was the 14th official census.
 
• __18th:__ There has been no 18th census yet, as the next scheduled census will be the 16th.

questions.question: If the Glycemic Index (GI) of a specific food is from 70 to 100, then the type of that food is:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**High-GI food**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Glycemic Index (GI)** is a numerical scale that measures how quickly a carbohydrate-containing food raises blood glucose levels after consumption.
 
• Foods are generally classified into three categories based on their GI values: **Low-GI**, **Medium-GI**, and **High-GI**.
 
• Foods with a GI value between **70 to 100** fall under the category of **High-GI foods**.
 
• High-GI foods cause a rapid spike in blood sugar levels because their carbohydrates are digested and absorbed quickly.
 
• Examples of High-GI foods include processed foods like **white bread**, **instant rice**, and **sugary beverages**.
 
• High-GI foods are beneficial in situations where quick energy is needed, such as during or after high-intensity exercise, but they are generally not recommended for people with conditions like **diabetes**.
 
• Understanding the GI of foods is crucial for maintaining healthy blood sugar levels and making informed dietary choices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Low-GI food**__

 __
 
• Low-GI foods have a GI value of **55 or less**.
 
• They cause a slow and steady increase in blood sugar levels and are ideal for people with **diabetes** or those looking to control their weight.
 
• Examples include **lentils**, **whole oats**, and **most fruits**.
 
 
 
• **Medium-GI food**__
 __
 
• Medium-GI foods have a GI value between **56 and 69**.
 
• These foods have a moderate impact on blood sugar levels and are considered a balanced option for energy.
 
• Examples include **brown rice**, **sweet potatoes**, and **whole wheat bread**.
 
 
 
• **Extremely low-GI food**__
 
 
• Foods with an extremely low GI value are generally rare and have a GI much lower than **55**.
 
• Examples may include foods that are non-carbohydrate-based, such as **meat**, **fish**, and **eggs**, which do not significantly affect blood sugar levels.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct postulates of Dalton's atomic theory?

A. All matter is made up of atoms. These atoms participate in chemical reactions.

B. Atoms might be created or destroyed during a chemical reaction.

C. Atoms of different elements vary in mass and chemical properties.

D. Compounds are combination of atoms in the ratio of whole or fractional numbers.

E. A compound will always have constant relative number and kind of atoms.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**A, C, E**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dalton's Atomic Theory** was one of the earliest theories to describe the structure and behavior of atoms.
 
• **Statement A:** "All matter is made up of atoms. These atoms participate in chemical reactions" aligns with Dalton's postulate that matter consists of indivisible particles called **atoms**. These atoms are fundamental building blocks and actively participate in chemical reactions, remaining unchanged.
 
• **Statement C:** "Atoms of different elements vary in mass and chemical properties" is correct as Dalton's theory suggested that atoms of each element are unique in their **mass** and **chemical behavior**.
 
• **Statement E:** "A compound will always have constant relative number and kind of atoms" refers to the law of **constant proportions**, which states that a chemical compound always contains its component elements in fixed ratios by mass.
 
• These statements reflect the foundational principles of Dalton's theory, which provided the basis for modern chemistry and atomic models.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Statement B:**__

 __
 
• This statement, "Atoms might be created or destroyed during a chemical reaction," contradicts Dalton's atomic theory. According to his postulates, **atoms cannot be created or destroyed** in chemical reactions; they only rearrange to form new substances.
 
• This concept is in line with the **law of conservation of mass**, which asserts that matter cannot be created or destroyed in a chemical reaction.
 
 
 
• **Statement D:**__
 __
 
• This statement, "Compounds are a combination of atoms in the ratio of whole or fractional numbers," is incorrect. Dalton proposed that atoms combine in **simple whole-number ratios** to form compounds, not fractional ratios.
 
• The presence of fractional numbers would violate Dalton's postulate of the indivisibility and discrete nature of atoms.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Dalton's Atomic Theory:**__
 
 
• It marked the beginning of modern atomic science and provided a scientific explanation for chemical reactions.
 
• The theory laid the groundwork for later discoveries, such as the structure of the atom and the periodic table.

questions.question: The famous Sanskrit grammar book 'Mahabhasya' was written by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Patanjali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahabhasya** is a commentary on Panini's grammar work **Ashtadhyayi**.
 
• It was written by the Sanskrit grammarian **Patanjali**, who is also believed to have lived around the 2nd century BCE.
 
• The **Mahabhasya** is considered one of the most significant works in the field of **Sanskrit grammar** and linguistics.
 
• This work not only explains Panini's rules but also provides **critical analysis, examples, and counterexamples** to clarify grammatical concepts.
 
• It is one of the three foundational works of Sanskrit grammar, along with **Panini's Ashtadhyayi** and **Katyayana's Varttikas**.
 
• The **Mahabhasya** played an essential role in preserving the structure of the Sanskrit language and influenced later grammatical traditions.
 
• Patanjali is also often associated with the **Yoga Sutras**, although the authorship of both works by the same person is debated.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bhartruhari**__

 __
 
• **Bhartruhari** was an Indian linguist, poet, and philosopher who lived during the **5th century CE**.
 
• He is well-known for his work on language and grammar, particularly the **Vakyapadiya**, which deals with the **philosophy of language**.
 
• The Vakyapadiya discusses the relationship between language, thought, and reality.
 
 
 
• **Vedvyas**__
 __
 
• **Vedvyas** is a central figure in Indian mythology, credited with composing the **Mahabharata**.
 
• He is also believed to have compiled the **Vedas** and written the **Puranas**.
 
• However, there is no evidence linking him to works on grammar.
 
 
 
• **Panini**__
 
 
• **Panini** was a renowned Sanskrit grammarian who lived during the **5th–4th century BCE**.
 
• He is best known for his work **Ashtadhyayi**, a treatise that systematized Sanskrit grammar.
 
• Panini laid the foundation for the grammatical tradition, which was later expanded by Patanjali in the **Mahabhasya**.
